[{"label":"A","letter":"A","text":"What is unit of excretory system?","marks":1,"answer":"Nephron is the functional unit or excretory system."},{"label":"B","letter":"B","text":"What do you mean by stomatal transpiration?","marks":2,"answer":"Transpiration is a physiological process by which water is carried through plants and then releases into the atmosphere. If this transpiration is occurred through stomata then it is called stomatal transpiration.
There are special openings with two guard cells in the leaves, young stems, sepals, and petals of flowers. These openings are called stomata. \(95\%\) of the total transpiration in a plant occurs through the stomata."},{"label":"C","letter":"C","text":"Explain the circulation of two gases by Fig.-Y mentioned organ.","marks":3,"answer":"Fig.- Y in the stem indicate heart. \(\mathrm{O_2}\) and \(\mathrm{CO_2}\) transportation is done by the circulatory system through two different process. One is pulmonary circulation and another one is systemic circulation.
Pulmonary circulation:
The pulmonary circulation is the part of the circulatory system in which oxygen-depleted blood is pumped away from the heart, via the pulmonary artery, to the lungs and returned, oxygenated, to the heart via the pulmonary vein.
Oxygen-deprived blood from the superior and inferior vena cava enters the right atrium of the heart and flows through the tricuspid valve (right atrioventricular valve) into the right ventricle, from which it is then pumped through the pulmonary semilunar valve into the pulmonary artery to the lungs. Gas exchange occurs in the lungs, whereby \(\mathrm{CO_2}\) is released from the blood, and oxygen is absorbed. The pulmonary vein returns the now oxygen-rich blood to the left atrium.
A separate circuit from the systemic circulation, the bronchial circulation supplies blood to the tissue of the larger airways of the lung.
Systemic circulation:
The systemic circulation is a circuit loop that delivers oxygenated blood from the left heart to the rest of the body through the aorta. Deoxygenated blood is returned in the systemic circulation to the right heart via two large veins, the inferior vena cava and superior vena cava, where it is pumped from the right atrium into the pulmonary circulation for oxygenation.
Thus, circulation of the two gases is done by the mentioned organ."},{"label":"D","letter":"D","text":"Describe one diseases with symptom, causes and remedy for "X" mentioned system.","marks":4,"answer":"The 'X' mentioned organ in the stem is Lungs. Lungs are the main organ of the respiratory system. The right and left lungs are situated on either side of the heart.
The organ can be damaged by the infection of virus or bacteria. One of the major disease of lung is bronchitis.
Causes:
The disease is caused by a bacterial infection. Living in unhealthy conditions, inhaling dust, polluted air, smoking cigarettes and cold are some of the reasons that may cause bronchitis. Once attacked by bronchitis there is every possibility of a frequent attack.
Symptoms:
- Clear, white, yellow or green mucus-stained cough.
- Chest pain when coughing.
- Shortness of breath.
- A sore throat.
- A runny nose.
- A high temperature.
Remedies: Preventive measures include:
- Stop smoking, drinking alcohol, use of tobacco.
- Follow treatment according to physician advice.
- Keep the patient in a tolerable temperature and dry environment.
- Feed nutritious liquid and hot food, e.g., hot milk, soup etc.
- Taking complete rest.
---"}]

Each nephron is composed of a renal corpuscle, or malpighian body and renal tubule. Each renal corpuscle is divided into two parts, the glomerulus and the Bowman's Capsule. The Bowman's capsule encloses the glomerulus. Each Bowman's capsule is a cup- shaped expanded organ, composed of two epithelial layers. Inside the Bowman's Capsule, there is a small cluster of blood vessels called the glomerulus. The glomerulus acts as a filter and produces filtrate from blood. The renal tubule is a long pipe- like structure containing the tubular fluid filtered through the glomerulus. Each renal tubules is divided into three regions; the proximal convoluted tubules, Henley's loop and the distal convoluted tubule."},{"label":"D","letter":"D","text":"How do you think the problem can be solved if the mentioned part 'A' is not working properly? When the kidneys are badly damaged or inactive, then the blood can be filtered by this dialysis method. Generally, dialysis is done by a dialysis machine. In this way, harmful nitrogenous waste is excreted out through dialysis machine. But this process is very expensive and time consuming. On the other hand, the second procedure is kidney transplantation. When the kidneys become damaged or inactive, they can be replaced by a healthy kidney of a healthy person. Kidney replacement can be done in two ways - a kidney taken from a close relative or from a dead person. A dead person would be a person who is brain dead but the organs are kept alive artificially. But, in both cases, before transplantation, matching of tissue is necessary. So, dialysis or transplantation procedure can be implemented in case of kidney is not working properly.\n---"}]

Explain.","marks":2,"answer":"For all physiological process, an adequate amount of water is necessary. When the water content in the body is more, most of the water is removed from the body as urine. When the water content of the body is less, the nephrons of the kidney maintain water equilibrium through reabsorption. Thus, maintaining the solute optimal concentration of body fluids is called osmoregulation."},{"label":"C","letter":"C","text":"Draw a labelled diagram of "X" organ in the stem.","marks":3,"answer":"The organ in the stem indicated by "X" is kidney. [Figure: Labelled diagram of human kidney]"},{"label":"D","letter":"D","text":"The system given in the stem plays important role in human body—Evaluate.","marks":4,"answer":"The system given in the stem represents human excretory system. It plays important role in the human body. This is evaluated below:
Excretory system helps remove the nitrogenous waste materials produced during metabolism inside the human body. These waste materials are commonly urea, uric acid, creatinine and various salts. These elements are poisonous and cause extreme harm to the body. Failure in excretion of these products results in deposition of them inside the body, which may initiate the onset of various diseases and may even lead to death. Nephrons of kidney helps to remove some of these wastes via producing urine continuously through a complex process. This urine reaches to the pelvis of the kidney through collecting tubules and proceeds through the funnel- like extended part of the pelvis and enters ureter. Ureter carries urine from kidney to urinary bladder. Urine is stored there for the time being. When the bladder is filled up with urine, a sensation of urination is created and allows urine to pass out of the body through urethra. In this way, waste materials are removed from the body through renal system.
---"}]

parts: [{"label":"A","letter":"A","text":"What is Bowman's capsule?","marks":1,"answer":"Bowman's capsule is a part of the nephron that is made up of two layers of epithelial cells arranged in a cup- like sack that surrounds the glomerulus."},{"label":"B","letter":"B","text":"Explain the importance of osmoregulation in human body.","marks":2,"answer":"For all physiological process, an adequate amount of water is necessary. When the water content in the body is more, most of the water is removed from the body as urine. When the water content of the body is less, the nephrons of the kidney maintain water equilibrium through reabsorption. In case of failure of the kidneys, water accumulates in the body. The whole body, including eyes and face, may swell up and it can create high blood pressure. So, the importance of osmoregulation in the human body is immense."},{"label":"C","letter":"C","text":"How the above figure \"W\" produce urine? Explain.","marks":3,"answer":"The figure \"W\" represents kidney. The formation of urine from kidney is explained below: The glomerulus acts as a filter and produces filtrate from blood. The liquid filtrate is called ultra- filtrate. This ultra- filtrate, when passing through the tubules, repeatedly goes through absorption and excretion. Finally, the liquid filtrate that remains is urine. This urine reaches the pelvis of the kidney through collecting tubules and proceeds through the funnel- like extended part of the pelvis and enters the ureter. The ureter carries urine to the urinary bladder, where it is stored temporarily. When the urinary bladder fills with urine, a sensation to urinate is created and allows urine to pass out of the body through the urethra. In this way, kidneys help expel nitrogenous waste product from the body."},{"label":"D","letter":"D","text":"If the above figure \"W\" will be fail in human body what are problem will arise? Analyze it.","marks":4,"answer":"The complications that would develop if the aforementioned figure \"W\", i.e., kidney fails in the human body, are analyzed below: Normal activities of kidney can be hampered due to malfunction of kidney. As a consequence, burning sensation of kidney, problems in urination and kidney stone may occur. The symptoms of kidney diseases are the whole body may swell up, loss of albumin during urination, urine with patches of blood, burning sensation during urination, urinating often, or in some cases urination reduced or stopped. Initially, the formation of kidney stones causes no remarkable problem. Problems occur when the stone goes downward into the ureter and obstructs urination. A very dull and steady pain in the lower back is the symptom of this disease. Blood passes into the urine. Kidney failure occurs gradually from diseases such as nephritis, diabetes, hypertension, stones, etc. Symptoms of kidney failure are difficulty in urination and increased level of creatinine in blood.\n---"}]

A longitudinal section of it is given below:\n[Diagram of longitudinal section of kidney with labels: Cortex, Medulla, Pelvis, Ureter, Renal Artery, Renal Vein]"},{"label":"D","letter":"D","text":"Analyze the role of figure 'X' in regulating the bodies excretion of harmful waste products and water balance.","marks":4,"answer":"Figure 'X' of the stem indicates the excretory system of human beings. Excretory system helps to eliminate the harmful nitrogenous substances from the human body and maintain the balance of water in the body. The waste products include urea, uric acid, creatinine and different kinds of salts. These substances are harmful and poisonous for the body. These substances are of no use for the body, but may cause various diseases if they remain inside the body for long. It can even cause death. However, the nephron inside the kidney is continuously producing urine in a complex process. Excessive water, salt, organic substances, vitamin, glucose and other harmful nitrogenous materials reaches the pelvis of the kidney through collecting tubules and proceeds through the funnel like extended part of the pelvis and enters the ureter. The ureter carries urine to the urinary bladder, where it is stored temporarily. When the urinary bladder fills with urine, a sensation to urinate is created and allows urine to pass out of the body through the urethra. The amount and concentration of water and salt in the organism is controlled in such a way that the overall osmotic pressure remains almost unchanged. This process is called osmoregulation or water equilibrium. Through excretion kidney removes the extra water from the body and keeps the equilibrium of water in the body. Thus, the figure 'X' of the stem indicating excretory system through urinating removes harmful wastes and through osmoregulation keeps the equilibrium of water.\n---"}]

parts: [{"label":"A","letter":"A","text":"What is the definition of renal tubule?","marks":1,"answer":"Urine passes to the ureter through the collecting tubules and finally deposits to the urinary bladder, which spreads up to the tubules called renal tubules."},{"label":"B","letter":"B","text":"Why do the fittest organism survive? Living organisms has to fight adverse environment for its survival. The animals which can survive the environment remains alive and the others become extinct. For example: desert animals have learnt to preserve water and they will survive in the future by adapting."},{"label":"C","letter":"C","text":"Describe the structure of 'A'.","marks":3,"answer":"A of the stem indicates kidney which acts as the filter of the body. The structure of kidney is mentioned below: The structure of kidney is like a bean seed and it is red in colour. The outer side of kidney is convex, and the inner side is concave with an indentation called the hilus or hilum. The ureter and renal vein comes out from the hilum and the renal artery enters the kidney. Two ureters arise from two kidney, proceeding downwards to open into the urinary bladder. The funnel shaped extended part (space) of the ureter is called the renal pelvis. Kidneys are enclosed with a special fibrous membrane called the renal capsule. Adjacent to the renal capsule is the cortex, and the inner side (part) is the medulla. Both of these regions are composed of connective tissues and blood vessels. Generally, there are 8- 12 renal pyramids in the medulla. The expanded apex of each pyramid is called renal papilla. These papilla project directly into the ureter. Each kidney contains a particular type of tubules called uriniferus tubules. Each uriniferous tubule has two parts, the nephron and the collecting tubule. Urine is produced in the nephron and the collecting tubules carry urine to the pelvis."},{"label":"D","letter":"D","text":"Evaluate the function of the organ mentioned in the stem to the release of nitrogenous waste products.","marks":4,"answer":"The mentioned organ in the stem is excretory organ, kidney of human body. The function of the organ mentioned in the stem to the release of nitrogenous waste products is described below: Kidney, ureter, urinary bladder etc. forms excretory system. Excretory system eliminates unnecessary and harmful nitrogenous waste products from the body. Excretory products with blood by the renal artery travels through the efferent arterials and enters glomerules. In a special process, except the blood vessels and plasma, the remaining parts are refined and deposited to the renal capsule. From there the deposited liquid flows through different capillaries. The nephron of kidney continuously produces urine in a complex process. At this time, the necessary elements of the body is reabsorbed from the filtrate. The produced urine reaches the pelvis through the collecting tubules. From pelvis the urine passes the funnel shaped structure of ureter and reaches the ureter. From ureter, urine reaches the urinary bladder and remains stored for some time. When the urinary bladder is filled with urine, there arises a desire to urinate and urine comes out through the hole under the urinary bladder. Thus, kidney expels harmful nitrogenous waste materials from the body. From the above discussion it can be said that, the mentioned organ of the stem, kidney helps to expel harmful nitrogenous waste materials from the body.\n---"}]

The kidneys separate nitrogenous waste products from the blood and send them to the bladder through urine. Urine contains nitrogenous waste products like urea, uric acid, ammonia, creatinine etc. They are very harmful to animals. Kidneys play a very important role in removing these unnecessary and harmful waste products. In this case, the renal capsule of the kidney acts as an ultrafilter. The process of transpiration takes place in plants and the process of excretion takes place in animals. When plants absorb water from the soil, they absorb more water than they need. This excess water is harmful to plants. In the process of transpiration, the plant expels this excess water \\((99\\%)\\) from its body by evaporation through various aerial organs. On the other hand, nitrogenous waste products are produced in various metabolic processes in the animal body. These substances are very harmful to animals. Kidneys produce urine in the process of excretion. Nitrogenous waste products are removed from the animal's body through the urine produced. As a result, the body is protected from the toxicity of harmful substances. Thus, it appears that both the processes are beneficial to the respective organisms and the processes are similar.\n---"}]

The glomerulus in the nephron acts as a filter to filter fluid from the blood. This liquid is called ultrafiltrate. As the ultrafiltrate flows through the renal tubule, it undergoes several more rounds of absorption and excretion. Evaluate.","marks":4,"answer":"Salim is suffering from kidney failure. The doctor suggested dialysis or kidney transplant. In dialysis, the blood is purified with the help of a dialysis machine. In this case, one end of the dialysis tube is connected to the artery of the patient's arm and the other end of the dialysis tube to the vein of the same arm. Before a kidney transplant, the donor and recipient tissue must be matched. Currently, millions of kidney failure patients in the world are being cured by adding or transplanting kidneys. So from the above discussion it can be said that kidney transplant procedure is more sustainable for Salim.\n---"}]

Give your opinion.","marks":4,"answer":"Mahin's kidney has been damaged. For kidney failure dialysis or kidney transplantation might be the treatment so that he can lead a healthy life. When the kidneys are badly damaged or inactive then the blood can be filtered (purified) by a scientific method called dialysis. Generally, it is done by a dialysis machine. Artery and veins of patient's same wrist are connected to the two ends of dialysis tubes. Blood from the artery passes into the dialysis tube. The wall of the tube is partially semipermeable, so urea, uric acid and other harmful substances are removed. Then the purified blood enters into patient's body through the vein. In this way, harmful nitrogenous waste is excreted out. But this process is very expensive and time consuming. Another treatment is kidney replaced by a healthy kidney of a healthy person especially from close relative or from a dead person. This is called transplantation. Millions of kidney failure patients get a healthy life by transplanting kidneys. Before transplantation matching of tissue is necessary. Only one kidney is enough for a person for one's survival. In our country kidney transplantation has been done very successfully. So, according to above information kidney transplantation treatment should be followed by Mahin to lead a healthy life.\n---"}]

Dialysis is a scientific method where blood is purified using a dialysis machine when kidneys are damaged. One end of the dialysis tube is connected to an artery and the other to a vein in the wrist. question: Sarmila is taking pain killers of arthritis from long days. Recently for less urination she goes to doctor and can know that in her blood creatinine level has increased and her one organ is damaged.
parts: [{"label":"A","letter":"A","text":"What is Nephron?","marks":1,"answer":"The Nephron is the functional unit of the kidney. Each kidney contains about 1 to 1.2 million Nephron units."},{"label":"B","letter":"B","text":"What is meant by Osmoregulation?","marks":2,"answer":"Osmoregulation is the active regulation of the osmotic pressure of an organism's body fluids. Water balance is maintained in the human body through osmoregulation. For all physiological processes, an adequate amount of water is necessary. Excessive water is removed from the body as urine. The main function of the kidney is to keep the balance of water. The Nephrons of the kidney maintain water equilibrium through reabsorption. Excretory fluids, water and other substances are filtered in the glomerulus. In failure of the kidneys, water accumulates in the body."},{"label":"C","letter":"C","text":"Draw a diagram of the discussed organ of the stem and label it.","marks":3,"answer":"[Figure: Labelled diagram of human kidney with labels: Cortex, Medulla, Pelvis, Ureter, Renal Artery, Renal Vein]"},{"label":"D","letter":"D","text":"Analyze the remedies for the development of Sarmila's physical condition.","marks":4,"answer":"Sarmila's condition indicates that one of her kidneys has failed. This is diagnosed by the increased level of creatinine in blood, accompanied by less urination. Most of the drug is metabolized in the liver and excreted through kidney. Pain medication can damage kidneys if taken for a long time, which happened in case of Sarmila. Once the kidney is damaged, it is kind of rare to reverse the condition. As possible treatment options or remedies, kidney transplant or dialysis maybe done. A dialysis machine mimics some of the functions of a human kidney. A primary job of kidneys is to remove urea and certain salts from blood so they can exit the body in urine. A dialysis machine removes blood from the patient and runs it through tubes made of a semi- porous membrane. On the outside of the tubes is a sterile solution made of water, sugars and other components. Certain substances including red blood cells, white blood cells, and other important blood components cannot fit through the pores in the membranes because those components are too large. The urea and salt, however, flow through membranes easily and are removed through the sterile solution. If dialysis is not possible, then kidney transplantation can be done. For kidney transplantation, a kidney donor with the same tissue type and blood type should be managed. Kidney diseases can be prevented by drinking enough water and keeping balanced amount of electrolytes in diet. Although long term medication for any previous condition can certainly affect kidneys.\n---"}]

Each nephron is made up of a very small filter, called a glomerulus, which is attached to a tubule. As blood passes through the nephron, fluid and waste products are filtered out. That is why kidney is called filter of the body."},{"label":"C","letter":"C","text":"Explain the structure of the organ given in the stem.","marks":3,"answer":"The organ mentioned in the stem is kidney. The structure of kidney is described below: Kidney is reddish in color and bean shaped. The outer side of the kidney is convex and inner side is concave having an indentation called hilus. The chamber in the hilus is called pelvis. Two ureters (urinary ducts) arise from the pelvis of each kidney and proceed downwards to enter into the urinary bladder. From the hilus the renal vein comes out and renal artery enters the kidney. Each kidney is enclosed by one type of fibrous membrane called capsule. Longitudinal cross- section of each kidney shows two regions, the outer one is cortex and part is inner medulla. Generally, there are 8- 12 renal pyramids in the medulla. The apex of each pyramid is called papilla. These papilla projects directly into the ureter. Each kidney contains a particular type of tubule called uriniferous tubule. Each uriniferous tubule has two parts- nephron and collecting tubule. Urine is produced in nephron and collecting tubules carry urine to the pelvis."},{"label":"D","letter":"D","text":"Analyze what is to be done if the organ of the stem is damaged.","marks":4,"answer":"If the kidney is damaged, two main treatments are available: dialysis and kidney transplantation. Dialysis involves using a machine to filter blood artificially. A dialysis machine is connected to the patient's bloodstream via tubes. Blood passes through a semipermeable membrane in the machine, where waste products diffuse into a dialysate fluid. This process must be repeated regularly and is costly and time-consuming. Kidney transplantation involves surgically placing a healthy kidney from a donor into the patient's body. The donor can be a living relative or a deceased person with tissue compatibility. Transplantation offers a more permanent solution and improves quality of life significantly. Therefore, kidney transplantation is generally preferred for long-term health, though dialysis is a vital temporary or supportive measure.\n---"}]

Excretion is a biological process through which nitrogenous waste products produced by different metabolic activities are excreted out. These waste materials include urea, uric acid, creatinine, and different types of salts. These materials are extremely harmful and toxic to the body. If for some reason they build up inside the body, they may cause various diseases and sometimes, even death. But the nephrons present in the kidney are continuously producing urine through a complex process. The nitrogenous waste materials and water, mineral salts, vitamins, and glucose are stored in the pelvis with the urine and then pass to the urinary bladder through the ureter. Again, chemical processes produce \\(\\mathrm{CO_2}\\) in the cells which the red blood corpuscles carry in the form of sodium bi- carbonate and expel in the form of expiration. The white blood corpuscles of the blood destroy germs with the help of the phagocytosis process. It increases the immunity of the body by producing antigens and antibodies.
